title: Indoor/Outdoor Communication Error
shortDescription: Indoor and outdoor units have lost communication on ComfortNet models.
fullDescription:
On communicating Amana AC systems (ComfortNet), E1 means the indoor control can no longer exchange data with the outdoor unit.

Causes include loose data wires, incorrect thermostat wiring, a tripped outdoor breaker, or a board fault.
safetyWarning: Shut off power at the disconnect before servicing outdoor wiring.

fixSteps.title: Check breakers
fixSteps.instruction: Verify both indoor and outdoor breakers are on.

fixSteps.title: Tighten data terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, check 1/2 and C connections at both units.

title: Indoor Coil Thermistor Fault
shortDescription: Indoor coil temperature sensor open or shorted.
fullDescription:
The indoor coil thermistor measures evaporator temperature for freeze protection and staging. Out-of-range values trigger E2.

Commonly loose plug, water-damaged sensor, or cut wire.
safetyWarning: Refrigerant lines are cold or pressurized - do not cut anywhere near tubing.

fixSteps.title: Reseat sensor plug
fixSteps.instruction: Open air handler, unplug and firmly reseat the coil sensor connector.

fixSteps.title: Measure resistance
fixSteps.instruction: At 77F, should read ~10k ohms. Replace if open.

whenToCallPro: If thermostat continues to error after sensor swap.

title: High Pressure Switch Trip
fullDescription:
Amana AC units have a high pressure switch (typically opens around 600 psi on R-410A). E3 indicates it tripped, shutting the compressor down.

Causes are dirty condenser, failed condenser fan, overcharge, or blocked airflow.
safetyWarning: Refrigerant work requires EPA 608 certification. Do not open the sealed system.

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, rinse coil from inside out with gentle water spray.

fixSteps.title: Verify fan operation
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm fan spins freely and runs when calling for cool.

whenToCallPro: Any refrigerant diagnosis or fan replacement.

title: Low Pressure Switch Trip
shortDescription: Low-side pressure has fallen below protection threshold.
fullDescription: Low pressure usually means refrigerant loss, iced indoor coil, or restricted airflow. Amana units lock out the compressor when this switch opens to protect from slugging and motor damage.
safetyWarning: Iced coil can leak large volumes of water; turn system to fan-only to thaw.

fixSteps.title: Change filter and thaw
fixSteps.instruction: Run fan-only until all ice clears, replace filter.

fixSteps.title: Schedule leak check
fixSteps.instruction: Call pro for refrigerant pressure measurement and leak search.

title: Outdoor Ambient Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor air temperature sensor reading out of range.
fullDescription: Used for staging and low-ambient lockout. Sensor open or shorted results in E5 and a staging fallback.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Locate outdoor sensor, inspect for damage, measure resistance.

title: Compressor Not Running
shortDescription: Compressor called but current sensor reads zero.
fullDescription: Board energized contactor but no current was detected in the compressor leg. Indicates open contactor, bad compressor, or blown fuse.
safetyWarning: High voltage at contactor. Lockout/tagout before testing.
symptoms: No cooling, outdoor fan may or may not run

fixSteps.title: Test contactor
fixSteps.instruction: With 24V applied, verify contacts pull in and pass 240V.

title: Outdoor Fan Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor fan not running or stalled.
fullDescription: E7 means the condenser fan motor is not operating correctly. Could be seized bearings, failed capacitor, or open winding.
safetyWarning: Never touch a spinning fan or energized capacitor.
symptoms: Compressor may trip on E3 shortly after

fixSteps.title: Discharge and test capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: After discharging, measure microfarads against label value.

title: Indoor Blower Fault
shortDescription: Blower motor not reporting RPM feedback.
fullDescription: Variable-speed ECM blower failed to respond to a speed command or is reporting stalled. Indoor airflow failure causes immediate cooling lockout.
safetyWarning: ECM modules store energy; wait 5 minutes after power off.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wheel
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, rotate wheel by hand to confirm free movement.

title: Discharge Temperature High
shortDescription: Compressor discharge line too hot - protection trip.
fullDescription: On inverter/variable-capacity Amana units, a discharge thermistor protects the compressor. Overheating can mean undercharge, superheat issues, or insufficient condenser airflow.
safetyWarning: Discharge lines reach scalding temperatures - do not touch.
symptoms: Cycles on and off in heat

title: Low Incoming Voltage
shortDescription: Line voltage below minimum for reliable compressor start.
fullDescription: Board measures incoming 240V and locks out if below ~197V. Utility issue, undersized wiring, or loose lug at disconnect.

causes.cause: Loose lugs at disconnect or panel

fixSteps.title: Measure voltage under load
fixSteps.instruction: With compressor running, measure L1-L2 at disconnect.
